summary: This bill prohibits federal officers from executing any warrant without first announcing their authority and purpose, and bars DOJ funding to state or local agencies that allow warrants to be served without such notice before forcible entry.

scores.thoughts: The bill conditions receipt of existing DOJ funds on compliance with the no-knock warrant prohibition but does not authorize new spending, alter appropriation levels, or expand/reduce overall government outlays. It is therefore unrelated to the size of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related matters.
The bill addresses warrants executed by law enforcement and has no connection to healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical policy.
The bill regulates execution of search warrants and does not mention firearms, gun ownership, or gun regulations.
The bill makes no reference to immigration, border policy, visas, or enforcement of immigration laws.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related medical procedures.
The bill applies to federal, state, and local law enforcement officers and does not affect military or defense appropriations or operations.
No environmental, energy, or climate provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address welfare programs, food assistance, housing aid, or any social safety-net benefits.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.

While the bill is named after Breonna Taylor (whose death occurred during a drug-related warrant), its text addresses only warrant procedures and does not alter drug laws, enforcement priorities, or decriminalization.

The bill's sole purpose is to prohibit no-knock warrants at the federal level and to withhold DOJ funds from state and local agencies that continue to use them. This directly restricts a controversial policing tactic and is a classic criminal-justice-reform measure aimed at changing law-enforcement practices rather than increasing policing powers or sentencing severity.
The bill contains no trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No fiscal, deficit, or debt-reduction measures are present.
The bill does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
The bill does not mention foreign aid, international assistance, or State Department programs.
No election administration, voting access, or voter-ID provisions are included.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data collection, or privacy standards.
No labor, union, or employment-law provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, anti-discrimination rules, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
